required_inputs: Measurand: the reported rolling-bearing vibration quantity, raw waveform or declared summary, with the source-declared physical unit preserved; do not assume acceleration or convert units.
Sensor provenance: sensor or transducer identity, channel and location, mounting, sensitivity or range, and traceable record-level provenance.
DAQ provenance: DAQ identity, channel configuration, sampling rate, filtering or anti-alias settings, timestamp or record identity, and file or metadata provenance.
Calibration trace: reference identity, certificate or version or date, corrections, valid calibration range, and calibration uncertainty linked to the measurand.
Operating-condition strata: speed, load, fault state or severity, rig or site, sensor position or mounting, batch, and time where declared.
Repeatability unit: repeated observations of the same bearing, specimen, or record unit under unchanged operator, instrument, mounting, and operating conditions.
Reproducibility factors: operator, instrument or DAQ, refit or mounting, batch, site or rig, and time; mark unavailable factors explicitly.
Uncertainty budget inputs: random and systematic components, distributions or bounds, correlations, calibration contributions, resolution, drift, sampling, and model-form terms.
Missingness record: field-level missingness, missingness mechanism when known, and missing-not-at-random risk; never fill missing evidence with inferred values.
Unit-consistency record: units retained from acquisition through processing and reported quantity, with sampling rate and frequency band checked and no implicit conversion.
Control and analysis context: experimental unit, response, intervention contrast, nuisance factors, and randomization or blocking decision for any authorized analysis.
incompatible_conditions: Missing, invalid, or untraceable sensor or DAQ provenance.
Missing or invalid measurand units, operating-condition strata, or record identity.
Missing calibration identity, valid range, correction or version or date, or calibration uncertainty.
Measurand or operating point outside the declared calibration range.
Unresolved repeatability or reproducibility factors or uncertainty-budget components required for the selected claim.
Unavailable facility, ethics, or specialist safety approval for any regulated or hazardous measurement.
Unit inconsistency, unsupported conversion, or missingness that prevents preservation of the metric experimental unit.

assumptions: Bind only selected claims C1 and C2 and their metrics M1 and M2; introduce no additional claim type or decision metric.

The measurand, response, and experimental unit are the source-declared vibration quantity, its reported unit, and one independently identifiable record or bearing-condition unit; independence is assumed only after checking repeated records.

The measurement chain is assumed stable, traceable, and sensitive enough for a meaningful effect only as a hypothesis to be checked; no empirical calibration, repeatability, reproducibility, or UQ success is assumed.
Operating-condition strata and nuisance factors are potential confounders; cross-dataset comparability and transfer remain hypotheses until decisive evidence.
Unverified apparatus behavior, scale-up, causal effects, and public-record completeness remain hypotheses or missing evidence.
baselines: Metadata-only reuse without an explicit calibration, R&R, and UQ screening step.
controls: Use the metadata-only reuse condition as the status-quo baseline and contrast it with traceability-first screening; this is a measurement-validity control, not a performance claim.

Block by declared speed, load, fault state or severity, rig or site, sensor position or mounting, batch, and time; preserve the independent record or bearing-condition unit and do not infer randomization from public order.
Use negative, positive, reference, blank, or sham controls only when explicitly documented; record an absent control as missing evidence rather than fabricate it.
procedure_outline: Use an advisory measurement model from measurand to sensor or transducer, calibration trace, DAQ, processing, and reported quantity, retaining units at every link.

Screen the selected record's declared sensor or DAQ provenance, units, sampling rate, operating-condition strata, mounting, and calibration fields; produce only a bounded completeness and missingness record.

Define repeatability as unchanged-condition repeats of the same experimental unit and separate reproducibility across operator, instrument or DAQ, refit or mounting, batch, site or rig, and time; report unavailable factors.
Construct the uncertainty budget from supported components, propagate it with measurement-model-appropriate semantics, and evaluate coverage only where the interval and experimental unit are defined.
Keep the outline advisory and confirmation-gated; do not collect data, download records, operate equipment, or claim empirical success.
uncertainty_handling: Use an explicit budget with random and systematic components, distributions or bounds, correlations, calibration uncertainty, sensor or DAQ resolution, drift, sampling, and model-form terms.

Separate aleatory variability from epistemic uncertainty, identify dominant components, and state whether interval coverage is nominal, confidence, or credible; do not label missing components as zero.

Propagate supported components through the measurement model, preserve units, and report M2 with its uncertainty and coverage semantics only for repeated-condition summaries with a defined experimental unit.
Treat calibration and repeatability or reproducibility evidence as provenance prerequisites; absent or invalid evidence remains missing and prevents empirical success claims.
Treat cross-dataset comparison and transfer of uncertainty as hypothetical unless unit, frequency-band, sampling, operating-condition, and measurement-chain compatibility is established.
validation_checks: Verify measurand and unit consistency from raw or semi-raw record through reported quantity; do not apply implicit unit conversions.
Check measurement range, sensor sensitivity, DAQ sampling and filtering, calibration identity, valid range, uncertainty, and calibration residuals where declared.
Check operating-condition strata, record identity, control behavior, and whether blocking or randomization preserves the independent experimental unit.
Check missingness, including missing-not-at-random risk, before computing either selected metric.
Check repeatability under unchanged conditions and reproducibility across each available factor; preserve not-available outcomes.
Check interval construction, uncertainty-budget coverage, and unit-consistent M1 and M2 aggregation; structural validation is offline contract evidence only.
Confirm that the source ledger contains only eligible verified round-two records at their mapped evidence basis.
failure_modes: Saturation or limited sensor sensitivity can truncate the measurand and inflate or deflate M1 or M2.
Drift or hysteresis can create time-dependent bias and make repeatability appear better or worse than it is.
Contamination, batch effects, or mounting changes can alter the signal while being misattributed to the bearing condition.
Confounding by speed, load, fault severity, rig, sensor position, or frequency band can invalidate the intervention comparison and cross-dataset interpretation.
Pseudo-replication can treat repeated windows or correlated records as independent units and make coverage or completeness appear stronger than supported.
Failed blinding, where relevant, can introduce operator or analyst effects into classification of metadata or condition strata.
Missing-not-at-random fields or records can bias completeness and uncertainty summaries toward better-documented cases.
Calibration extrapolation beyond the declared valid range can invalidate the measurand and any associated uncertainty bound.
safety_boundaries: Do not operate equipment, collect specimens, download data, start services, upload research materials, or allocate resources under this bounded card.

Require qualified laboratory or domain review and facility, legal, and ethical approval for hazardous materials, radiation, pressure, high voltage, biological exposure, human participants, destructive testing, or regulated measurements.
Treat safety, regulatory, and operational conclusions as specialist-review boundaries; no safety conclusion follows from this card or its source ledger.
If safety approval or required specialist review is unavailable, the condition is incompatible and the card does not authorize work.
